content:
LAREDO, Texas — The death of a Dallas-area lawful permanent resident inside a federal immigration facility in Laredo has become a clash of stories.

Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, 56, was found unresponsive in his bed on Saturday morning, October 17, during a security check at the Rio Grande Processing Center, according to the Department of Homeland Security. Staff performed CPR and called emergency services, but he was pronounced dead roughly 20 minutes later. His cause of death remains unknown, with an autopsy pending at the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office.

What happened before staff found him is now the center of the dispute. DHS says Andrade-Covarrubias — who had diabetes, high blood pressure, and a heart condition — received proper medical care and was seen by medical professionals. But in a GoFundMe post, his family disputes that, FOX 4 Dallas reported.

His daughter, Estefani Andrade, 29, a U.S. citizen, told The Texas Tribune that her father brought his medications with him when he was detained and that facility staff would not "give him his medications." She said he reported trouble breathing and tightness in his chest, and told her the medical staff would "just ignore him."

Cuellar toured the facility Sunday

U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Laredo, toured the Rio Grande Processing Center on Sunday, October 18. He said he saw doctors, nurses, and medical equipment — but could not verify what treatment Andrade-Covarrubias actually received.

"Now I do have a couple audios from people that said that he was asking for medicine and that he was not given the medicine. So again, there's, you know, one side has one story. The other person has another story," Cuellar told FOX 4.

Cuellar said he has sent ICE written questions about the case and has requested surveillance video and medical records. Facility staff declined to provide specific details about Andrade-Covarrubias's case because the death remains under investigation, according to the Tribune.

"I can't make any promises, but I did talk to the wife a few minutes ago, and I told her that I would do everything I can as a member of Congress in the Homeland Appropriations to get her the transparency and the questions that she has," Cuellar said. "Any death in federal custody is a serious matter, and we need to know what happened."

Why he was detained

ICE said Andrade-Covarrubias was detained June 26 at a Laredo port of entry while returning to Texas from Mexico. According to the agency, officers believed he obtained his legal status fraudulently because he allegedly failed to disclose a 2004 arrest for theft when applying. That is an ICE allegation, not a proven finding. The agency did not say whether he was ever convicted, and his daughter told the Tribune that her father did disclose his criminal record during the application process — and that immigration officials approved his green card application.

ICE also said he was in removal proceedings before an immigration judge, with a hearing scheduled for November 2. He never made it there.

Andrade-Covarrubias had lived in the Dallas area for decades, working as a contractor painting apartments and townhomes. He raised three adult children, all born in the United States. His daughter said he traveled frequently to Mexico, where he was building a house he planned to settle in.

The family learned of the death from the county morgue

In another sign of how the case has been handled, the family says no federal agency contacted them directly. Estefani Andrade said they learned of her father's death from the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office. Mexico's Foreign Ministry, meanwhile, said ICE notified the Mexican consulate in Laredo, which then contacted the family — and Mexico has demanded a "prompt, thorough, and transparent" investigation, calling Andrade-Covarrubias the 18th Mexican national to die in U.S. custody or immigration operations since January 20, 2025.

What we are watching

Andrade-Covarrubias is the seventh person to die in ICE custody in Texas this year, and the second to die at an ICE facility in Laredo — following 63-year-old Felix Alcorta-Rodriguez, who died June 19 at the Webb County Detention Center. The facility is operated by the GEO Group under contract with ICE; FOX 4 reported the company referred its questions to DHS.

This is the watchdog question that matters: who independently verifies what happens inside that building? Cuellar's written questions and requests for surveillance video and medical records are a start, but so far no independent investigation has been announced. ICE's standard internal detention-death reviews remain exactly that — internal. The public evidence that could settle the family's claims — the surveillance footage, the medical records, the autopsy — has not been released.

A congressman says he has recordings of people saying a man with a heart condition asked for his medicine and did not get it. A daughter says her father called her from detention saying staff ignored him. The agency says the care was proper. The autopsy is pending. Webb Watch 956 will keep following this until the answers arrive.

Sources:

  • FOX 4 News — "Family demands answers after Dallas man dies in Laredo immigration detention"
  • US Border News (republishing The Texas Tribune) — "Dead man in Texas ICE facility was Lawful Permanent Resident"
  • Demócrata — "Mexico demands the US to clarify the death of a migrant in ICE custody in Texas"
  • The Texas Informer — "Tragic Discovery: Migrant Found Deceased at Laredo ICE Facility"
  • TMJ4 / Scripps News — "ICE detainee found dead in private lockup was a legal permanent resident," Oct. 20, 2026
  • PULSO MX — "Muere mexicano bajo custodia del ICE en Texas," Oct. 20, 2026

Update — October 20, 2026

New facts emerged Tuesday about the facility where Andrade-Covarrubias died. Scripps News reported that ICE's own January 2025 Office of Detention Oversight inspection of the Rio Grande Processing Center found the facility did not always complete health assessments for newly detained people within the two weeks required by national detention standards. The inspection report rated the facility "good" overall, according to the Scripps report. The finding is relevant because the family's central claim is that the detainee's medical needs were ignored — a claim ICE disputes.

Separately, the detainee's daughter, Estefani Andrade, has launched a fundraiser to pay for her father's funeral, according to PULSO MX, which quoted the family saying: "We believe he did not receive the medical attention he so desperately needed."

For the latest on ICE's official statement on the death, Rep. Henry Cuellar's seven written questions, and the notification of federal oversight agencies, see our follow-up story: ICE Says Detainee Who Died in Laredo Got Proper Medical Care; Family Disputes It as Cuellar Demands Answers. The autopsy from the Webb County Medical Examiner's Office was still pending as of October 20.

Update — October 22, 2026

The Webb County medical examiner’s findings became public — at least in part. Local broadcaster KGNS reported Oct. 19 that the medical examiner’s office had classified Andrade-Covarrubias’s death as natural. The family disputes that account: his daughter, Estefani Andrade, alleges staff withheld his heart and diabetes medication — a claim ICE denies, saying in an Oct. 20 statement that he received proper medical care and that the cause of death was still pending the autopsy. Separately, on Oct. 20, Mexican Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco said Mexico would seek a meeting with ICE this week, raise the case with the U.S. State Department and the Department of Homeland Security, and file the promised formal complaint with the Webb County district attorney this week; as of this update, the filing had not been publicly confirmed. Velasco said he had spoken with the detainee’s widow, who described her husband as a lawful U.S. resident. Webb Watch will keep watching for confirmation of the filing and the full autopsy report.

Sources update: Medical Daily (UK), Oct. 21, 2026 (citing KGNS, Oct. 19); USA Today, Oct. 21, 2026; EFE via la Voz del Quequén, Oct. 20, 2026; San Antonio Current.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Family of Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, 56, disputes DHS claims he received proper care before dying at the Rio Grande Processing Center. Rep. Cuellar says he has recordings of people saying the detainee asked for medicine and was denied.
title: ICE Death in Laredo Turns Into Dispute: Family Challenges DHS Care Claims After Andrade-Covarrubias Dies in Custody
